_**User**_

.md files: Is it possible to add a comment as in pdfs?

---

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Considering whether markdown files support comments similar to PDFs.

Markdown supports HTML comments (`<!-- comment -->`) that render invisibly. These differ from PDF reviewer annotations.

Native markdown lacks PDF-style sticky annotations. GitHub pull request reviews and IDE tools like Cursor or VS Code offer alternative ways to leave reviewer-style comments.
</details></think>

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

Not in the same way as PDF annotations.

Markdown has no built-in sticky-note / review-comment layer like Acrobat or Preview. What you *can* do:

1. **Invisible HTML comments** (common in `.md`):
   ```markdown
   <!-- TODO: check this number -->
   ```
   They don’t show in most rendered previews (GitHub, VS Code preview, etc.), but anyone editing the file can see them.

2. **Visible inline notes** in the body, e.g. `> **Comment:** …` or `[comment]: # (…)` — visible to readers unless you strip them later.

3. **Review outside the file**: PR review comments on GitHub, or comments in Notion/Google Docs if you paste the content there.

So: you can leave hidden notes with `<!-- … -->`, but not PDF-style floating review comments on the rendered page.

_**Agent (grok-4.5)**_

Use this syntax:

```markdown
![alt text](path/or/url/to/image.png)
```

For your local plot, from `2026-07-20-incidents-key-findings.md`:

```markdown
![Weekly incidents by model type](2026-07-22-analyse/weekly_incidents_overall_model_type.png)
```

Optional size control isn’t standard Markdown; in many renderers (including VS Code / GitHub) you can use HTML instead:

```html
<img src="2026-07-22-analyse/weekly_incidents_overall_model_type.png" alt="Weekly incidents" width="600"/>
```
